title: Which Body Module Controls What?
introduction:
I use these lists as a responsibility map for the Mustang's body electronics. The BCM and BCM-B have separate desks on the same switchboard, so the module names are worth keeping straight—especially when several lighting functions appear together.

Find the function under its named controller, and retain the convertible qualifications. This overview identifies control responsibilities. A symptom under a module's heading does not, by itself, establish that the module has failed; power, connections and shared information can also matter.

The BCM coordinates the functions below. I use this list to identify its responsibilities before looking for a function-specific explanation or diagnostic test.
edits.why: A controller can coordinate a function using information from elsewhere in the vehicle; ownership of the function is not proof of a faulty controller.

edits.text: Remote keyless entry: RKE system control

edits.why: Wheel-mounted sensors transmit by radio to a radio transceiver module, which passes information to the body controller. This illustrates how control responsibility can include information gathered by other components.

edits.text: Functions of Body Control Module B (BCM-B)
Body Control Module B (BCM-B) coordinates the functions below. Read these as its own responsibilities, including the entries specifically qualified for convertible vehicles.
edits.why: The similar controller names should not blur the division of functions.
Inhibit means preventing the function from operating. This entry identifies responsibility without specifying the conditions that trigger inhibition.
